prerequisites: Electric circuits and elementary electronic devices: General electronics.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of logic gates, Boolean algebra, and combinatorial and sequential logic circuits
Knowledge of the issues underlying the timing of simple sequential circuits
Knowledge of the main digital electronic devices and their main operational and functional characteristics
Understanding of digital circuit synthesis and analysis methods
Understanding of power consumption issues in digital circuits
Knowledge of the main A/D and D/A conversion methods
Ability to interpret datasheets of digital integrated circuits
Ability to evaluate the main factors contributing to the performance of a digital system
Ability to evaluate the speed limits of a digital system
Ability to design digital systems of moderate complexity
Ability to evaluate, also with an experimental approach, the performance of a digital system
Ability to analyze and evaluate the specifications of simple electronic devices
Ability to process and interpret experimental data obtained from laboratory measurements, in order to formulate well-reasoned judgments
Ability to integrate, collaborate and communicate in group work dynamics through experimental laboratory activities
Ability to clearly and logically express the considerations underlying the design of digital circuits to specialized and non-specialized people
Ability to independently retrieve and understand technical documentation on electronic devices
Ability to independently draw up the list of specifications for a digital system of moderate complexity

syllabus_topics: Fundamental characteristics of integrated circuits used in digital systems
Laboratory exercises aimed at verifying the performance of logic networks
Timing of circuits based on buffers, bus-switch, registers, latches, counters, memories
teaching_methods: Frontal lectures with slide projection and blackboard integration
Examples and exercises at the blackboard
Seminars given by companies in the field of electronic device development
Laboratory activities (12 h) aimed at evaluating the behavior and performance of simple combinatorial/sequential circuits
Use of educational software for digital circuit simulation
Use of interactive "Student response system" applications
assessment_rules: The first exam session after the course concludes includes a written test, while subsequent sessions involve oral exams. Both types of exams consist of open questions and exercises to verify knowledge, comprehension, application abilities, judgment autonomy, communication skills, and learning abilities. Evaluation criteria range from 'Insufficient' for severe conceptual errors to 'Excellent' (29-30 cum laude) for comprehensive, in-depth knowledge and critical thinking. 'La Lode' (cum laude) is awarded for brilliant and original work.

Horowitz, Hill, "L'arte dell'elettronica", Zanichelli ed., 2018 (general reference text)
P.Spirito: Elettronica Digitale, 2nd-3rd ed, McGraw Hill, (support for digital circuits description)
Data sheets and application notes of logic integrated circuits
